name: revshell
description: Multi-session reverse shell handler + payload generator. Python port of OnlyShell with 25+ language payloads, TLS, session stabilizer, and command broadcasting.
author: 0xb0rn3 | github.com/0xb0rn3

optional_dependencies.nc / ncat / socat: For generated payload options — not required by the handler itself

help.description: Feature-complete Python port of OnlyShell (github.com/malwarekid/OnlyShell). Accepts unlimited simultaneous reverse shell connections, auto-detects shell type (bash/powershell/cmd/zsh/sh) and OS, supports backgrounding sessions, broadcasting commands, TLS-encrypted listeners, PTY stabilization, and session output buffering. Also generates 30+ ready-to-paste reverse shell payloads for bash, python, perl, ruby, php, nodejs, go, awk, lua, java, PowerShell, netcat, socat, and msfvenom stagers.

serve.description: Interactive OnlyShell-style TUI handler. Runs indefinitely accepting shells. Output goes to stdout directly (not JSON). Supports all sub-commands: list, interact, exec-all, stabilize, session, listen, listeners, cleanup.

listen.description: Headless listener — starts on port(s), collects shells for duration seconds, optionally runs initial_cmd on each, returns JSON report with all session details.

generate.description: Generate reverse shell one-liner payloads for a given LHOST:LPORT. Returns all 30+ payloads or a specific one.

check.description: Report which helper tools (nc, socat, python3, perl, ruby, php, node, msfvenom, etc.) are installed.

serve_commands.list: List all connected shells with ID, hostname, shell type, OS, remote address, and status (Active/Stale/Dead)
serve_commands.interact <id>: Drop into interactive session with shell. Inside: 'bg'/'background' to background, 'exit' to close shell.
serve_commands.exec-all <cmd>: Broadcast a command to all currently active shells simultaneously
serve_commands.stabilize <id>: Attempt PTY upgrade via python3 pty.spawn or script(1), then set TERM and stty
serve_commands.session <id>: Print buffered output captured from a backgrounded shell
serve_commands.listen <port[,port]>: Start additional listener(s) at runtime without stopping existing ones
serve_commands.listeners: Show all currently active listening ports
serve_commands.cleanup: Remove dead/disconnected shells from the session list
serve_commands.exit / quit: Shutdown the handler (does not kill connected shells)

shell_status.Active: Connected and responsive — seen within last 60 seconds
shell_status.Stale: No activity for more than 60 seconds — may still be alive

examples: nim_backdoor — compile a Nim reverse shell binary with reconnect loop (requires nim compiler)

lhost.description: IP address to bind listeners or embed in generated payloads
lhost.required: for generate mode; optional for listen/serve (default 0.0.0.0)

lport.description: Port to embed in generated payloads (generate mode)

duration.description: How long (seconds) to listen in headless listen mode before returning

initial_cmd.description: Command to run on each new shell immediately after connect (listen mode); output captured in session result

max_sessions.description: Stop listening after this many shells connect (0 = unlimited)

tls_cert.description: Path to TLS certificate file (.pem) for encrypted listener

tls_key.description: Path to TLS private key file (.pem) for encrypted listener

shell.description: Specific payload type to generate (generate mode). 'all' returns every payload.

target_os.description: Target OS for nim_backdoor: linux or windows

output.description: Output binary name for nim_backdoor (default: backdoor_<os>)

examples.description: Interactive handler via secV on multiple ports
Headless: catch one shell in 120s and run 'id; uname -a'
Generate TLS self-signed cert for encrypted listener
Check which payload helper tools are installed
Compile Nim reverse shell backdoor for Linux

features: Auto-detects shell type: bash, zsh, sh, PowerShell, cmd
Background/foreground session management without losing connection
Silent keepalive (bash no-op ':') — does not pollute shell output
Command broadcast to all active shells (exec-all)
PTY stabilizer: python3 pty.spawn + script(1) fallback + TERM/stty setup
Session output buffering for backgrounded shells
Multiple listeners on different ports, addable at runtime
30+ reverse shell payloads: bash, python, perl, ruby, php, nodejs, go, awk, lua, java, PowerShell (plain + b64), netcat, socat, msfvenom stagers
Listener hint printed alongside each generated payload
notes: AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED: Only use against systems you own or have explicit written permission to test
serve mode outputs directly to the terminal (not JSON) — use it from CLI or terminal tab in the GUI
listen mode is the JSON-friendly mode — use it from the GUI for automated workflows
For a stable interactive shell, run stabilize <id> after receiving the connection
TLS listener requires a cert+key pair — generate with: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 -nodes
Payloads with mkfifo or /tmp paths may require cleanup on the target after the session
